title: Parse a port number safely
description:
Write a parser that reports **why** it failed:

```c
enum port_error { PORT_OK = 0, PORT_EMPTY, PORT_NOT_A_NUMBER, PORT_OUT_OF_RANGE };

enum port_error parse_port(const char *text, int *out);   /* 1 to 65535; *out is only set on PORT_OK */
const char *port_error_text(enum port_error e);           /* "ok", "empty", "not a number", "out of range" */
```

Leading and trailing spaces are allowed (`" 8080 "`); anything else after the digits, or a sign, makes it `PORT_NOT_A_NUMBER`. Use `strtol` and check `errno` for numbers too large for a `long`.
hints: `strtol(text, &end, 10)` tells you where it stopped: if `end` (after skipping spaces) is not at the terminating zero, something other than digits followed. Set `errno = 0` before the call so `ERANGE` afterwards really comes from it.
`strtol` accepts a sign, but a port must not have one: check that the first non-space character is a digit before calling it.
